questions.prompt: Which Pillar 1 subtopic carries the [KEY] marker and is covered by 3B1B Chapter 6?
questions.explanation: Attention: Q/K/V, masking, multi-head is marked [KEY]; taught in Ch.6 Attention, step-by-step - 3B1B.

questions.prompt: Per the Pillar 1 gap-fill callout, why must positional encoding be injected into transformer inputs?
options: Because token order matters and attention alone does not encode position
questions.explanation: Gap fill: positional encoding injects order; learn it via Karpathy's Let's build GPT from scratch.

questions.prompt: Which often-skipped topic does the roadmap highlight about where an LLM stores factual knowledge?
options: Facts live only in attention heads
Facts are stored in the tokenizer
Facts sit in the final softmax layer
questions.explanation: Gap fill says MLP/feed-forward layers store factual knowledge; see Ch.7 How might LLMs store facts - 3B1B.

questions.prompt: According to the gap-fill warning, learners who watch only the attention video miss which two topics?
options: Positional encoding and fact storage in MLP layers
questions.explanation: Gap fill: most watch only attention; add positional encoding (Karpathy) and MLP fact storage (3B1B Ch.7).

questions.prompt: Which chapter covers the full forward pass, embeddings, and softmax?
options: Ch.5 Transformers, the tech behind LLMs - 3B1B
Ch.7 How might LLMs store facts - 3B1B
questions.explanation: Ch.5 Transformers, the tech behind LLMs (27m) covers forward pass, embeddings, softmax.

questions.prompt: In the roadmap, Tokenization/BPE plus positional encoding are assigned to which resource?
options: Karpathy - Let's build GPT from scratch
questions.explanation: Tokenization/BPE and positional encoding map to Karpathy's Let's build GPT from scratch (1h56m).

questions.prompt: What does the roadmap advise regarding 3B1B Chapters 1-4?
options: Skip unless you want neural-net basics/backprop; not needed to build
They are mandatory prerequisites for attention
questions.explanation: Gap fill: skip 3B1B Ch.1-4 (neural-net basics/backprop) unless wanted - not needed to build.

questions.prompt: Which resource does the roadmap assign to the big-picture subtopic of what an LLM is?
options: Karpathy - Let's build GPT from scratch
questions.explanation: Big-picture subtopic maps to LLMs explained briefly, the 8-minute 3Blue1Brown playlist.

questions.prompt: How does the roadmap phrase the goal of Pillar 2, LLM App Fundamentals?
options: From calling an API to shipping an LLM feature
From prompt engineering to model training
From Python basics to GPU clusters
questions.explanation: Pillar 2 goal: go from calling an API to shipping an LLM feature, via Ed Donner's LLM Engineering course.

questions.prompt: Why does an app use tool/function calling?
options: To let the model request external function calls so it can act on real data and systems
To fine-tune on new data mid-conversation
questions.explanation: Tool/function calling lets a model invoke external functions; covered in Ed Donner Wk2 plus a ReAct explainer.

questions.prompt: Which library does the roadmap name for building fast UIs in Pillar 2?
questions.explanation: Fast UIs subtopic names Gradio, taught in Ed Donner LLM Engineering Wk2.

questions.prompt: Which week of Ed Donner's course covers open-source models and HuggingFace?
questions.explanation: Open-source models and HuggingFace are scheduled in Ed Donner LLM Engineering Wk3.

questions.prompt: Per the roadmap, how should model selection be done in Wk4?
questions.explanation: Model selection / leaderboards is the Wk4 topic in Ed Donner LLM Engineering.

questions.prompt: Structured output in Pillar 2 relies on which formats and resource?
questions.explanation: Structured output means JSON with Pydantic; see Structured outputs - OpenAI docs.

questions.prompt: What does the roadmap say makes Ed Donner's course well suited for this pillar?
options: It focuses exclusively on vision models
questions.explanation: Pillar 2 intro: Ed Donner's course is strongest here because it is Ollama-first and laptop-friendly.

questions.prompt: Which topics fall under Ed Donner Wks 1-2 per the roadmap?
questions.explanation: Wks 1-2 cover APIs, prompts, streaming, multi-provider; Ed Donner LLM Engineering (repo).

questions.prompt: Which Pillar 3 foundations subtopic carries the [KEY] marker?
options: Why RAG; embeddings; vector DB; cosine similarity
questions.explanation: Foundations [KEY]: why RAG, embeddings, vector DB, cosine similarity; RAG from First Principles - Ankit Bansal (38m).

questions.prompt: What components make up hybrid retrieval as described in the roadmap?
options: BM25 keyword search plus dense embeddings, fused using reciprocal rank fusion (RRF)
questions.explanation: Hybrid search = BM25 + dense + RRF; see Production RAG w/ LangChain and Vector DBs - freeCodeCamp (7h38m).

questions.prompt: Which techniques does the roadmap list under reranking?
questions.explanation: Reranking uses cross-encoders or ColBERT; see Advanced RAG techniques - Field Guide to AI (9m read).

questions.prompt: HyDE and multi-query belong to which category of advanced RAG techniques?
questions.explanation: HyDE and multi-query are query transforms; see Advanced RAG: hybrid, reranking, query expansion.

questions.prompt: Which chunking strategies does the roadmap name as advanced alternatives?
questions.explanation: Advanced chunking = parent-child and sentence-window; see 12 Advanced RAG Techniques (2026) - Atlan.

questions.prompt: Per the roadmap rule of thumb, which RAGAS metrics measure retrieval quality rather than generation quality?
questions.explanation: Measure retrieval via context precision/recall separately from generation faithfulness; RAGAS explained - Logical Lenses.

questions.prompt: Per the gap-fill callout, how much does hybrid search plus reranking lift factual accuracy over basic embed-and-top-k RAG?
options: From 44% toward about 63% on the CRAG benchmark
questions.explanation: Gap fill cites CRAG benchmark: basic RAG scores roughly 44%; hybrid search plus reranking pushes toward 63%.

questions.prompt: The roadmap says do NOT ship RAG without three things. Which set is correct?
options: A larger model, longer prompts, more tokens
A reranker, hybrid BM25+dense retrieval, and a RAGAS eval harness run in CI on every change
questions.explanation: Gap fill ship checklist: reranker, hybrid (BM25+dense) retrieval, RAGAS eval harness in CI on every change.

questions.prompt: What is the one rule of fine-tuning marked [KEY] in Pillar 4?
questions.explanation: [KEY] rule from How to Fine-Tune an LLM (2026): fine-tune equals behavior, not knowledge.

questions.prompt: For fresh or frequently changing facts that need citations, which approach does the gap-fill callout recommend?
questions.explanation: Gap fill: RAG for fresh/changing facts and citations; never fine-tune to teach your documents.

questions.prompt: According to the roadmap, fine-tuning is the right tool for which goals?
options: Format, tone, domain vocabulary, and reasoning style
questions.explanation: Gap fill: fine-tune for format, tone, domain vocabulary, reasoning style; facts stay with RAG.

questions.prompt: What anti-pattern does the gap-fill callout explicitly warn against?
options: Fine-tuning to teach the model your documents
questions.explanation: Gap fill: never fine-tune to teach it your documents - that is knowledge, not behavior.

questions.prompt: What does QLoRA specifically involve per the roadmap?
options: A frozen base quantized to 4-bit NF4 plus small trainable low-rank adapters on attention projections
Distilling into a smaller student model
questions.explanation: Gap fill: QLoRA = 4-bit NF4 frozen base plus trainable low-rank adapters on attention projections; Mark Hennings - LoRA & QLoRA In-Depth.

questions.prompt: Which LoRA hyperparameters does the roadmap highlight?
questions.explanation: Subtopic lists rank, alpha, dropout, 4-bit NF4; see Mark Hennings - LoRA & QLoRA In-Depth (15m).

questions.prompt: Which three PEFT methods does the quick overview group together?
questions.explanation: Quick PEFT overview covers LoRA, QLoRA, DoRA; see PEFT Explained - Arivu (4m).

questions.prompt: How does the roadmap characterize fine-tuning's importance for typical app work?
options: Optional for most app work but a common interview topic
questions.explanation: Pillar 4 goal: know when NOT to fine-tune; optional for most app work yet a common interview topic; practiced in Ed Donner Wks 6-7.

questions.prompt: Which distinction is marked [KEY] in Jeff Su's AI Agents, Clearly Explained?
options: Agent vs workflow: agents choose their own steps and tools; workflows follow fixed developer-defined paths
questions.explanation: [KEY] subtopic Agent vs workflow plus ReAct loop comes from AI Agents, Clearly Explained - Jeff Su (10m).

questions.prompt: What is the core loop of the ReAct pattern?
options: Reason about a step, take an action with a tool, observe results, repeat until done
questions.explanation: ReAct interleaves reasoning and acting; see ReAct Agents, clearly explained - Akshay Pachaar (6m).

questions.prompt: Andrew Ng's Agentic AI course, marked [KEY], covers which four design patterns plus evals?
questions.explanation: Agentic AI - Andrew Ng, DeepLearning.AI (7h45m) [KEY] teaches reflection, tool use, planning, multi-agent patterns plus evals.

questions.prompt: Per the roadmap's module mapping, which module covers which pattern?
options: Module 1 Planning, Module 2 Reflection, Module 3 Tool use, Module 5 Multi-agent
Module 1 Multi-agent, Module 2 Planning, Module 3 Reflection, Module 5 Tool use
Module 1 Tool use, Module 2 Multi-agent, Module 3 Planning, Module 5 Reflection
All four patterns appear in Module 1 only
questions.explanation: Roadmap maps Reflection/Tool use/Planning/Multi-agent to Modules 2/3/1/5 of Andrew Ng's course respectively.

questions.prompt: Why does the roadmap place Andrew Ng's vendor-neutral course before framework tutorials like LangChain or CrewAI?
options: Because frameworks require paid licenses first
To understand agents from first principles before learning tools that implement the patterns
questions.explanation: Pillar 5 goal: understand agents from first principles, vendor-neutral, before frameworks; Andrew Ng's course is the backbone.

questions.prompt: Besides the four design patterns, what other major skill does Andrew Ng's course include per its [KEY] row?
questions.explanation: Row reads 4 patterns + evals (whole course) [KEY]: Agentic AI - Andrew Ng, DeepLearning.AI.

questions.prompt: Which resource supports building 8 agent projects in Pillar 5?
options: Ankit Bansal - RAG from First Principles
questions.explanation: Build 8 agent projects maps to Ed Donner - Agentic AI Engineering (Udemy, repo).

questions.prompt: What estimated length and role does the roadmap give Andrew Ng's Agentic AI course within Pillar 5?
options: Backbone of the pillar at roughly 7h45m including modules and notes repo
questions.explanation: Roadmap lists Agentic AI - Andrew Ng at 7h45m as the whole-course [KEY] backbone covering patterns, evals, modules.
